text:
Ten minutes and 11 seconds in, Buffalo had three goals on five shots and Logan Thompson was on the bench. Jack Quinn scored first, Rasmus Dahlin banked in a wraparound on the power play, and Beck Malenstyn added a backhand 25 seconds later. The Sabres went on to win 6-3 at Capital One Arena, snapping a five-game winless run (0-4-1) and handing Washington its fourth straight loss.

The night's history belonged to the losing side. Alex Ovechkin's assist on Boone Jenner's goal in the third was the 763rd of his career, passing Nicklas Backstrom's Capitals record of 762, as Tom Gulitti of NHL.com noted. It came in a season full of farewells, with teams around the league marking his final visits, and it is a record that once seemed to belong to Backstrom for good.

The scoreboard and the chances told different stories. Washington outshot Buffalo 37-18, took 72 shot attempts to 37, and finished with 4.57 expected goals (the quality of chances) to Buffalo's 3.25. Our replays of every shot gave the Capitals the win 87% of the time. Most of that came in a third period when Washington put up 2.99 expected goals, with Ryan Leonard scoring on the power play at 8:52 and Jenner 52 seconds later. By then it was 5-1, after Zach Benson and Tage Thompson had scored, and Quinn finished it with an empty-net goal at 19:17.

Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen is the reason the comeback stopped at two. A week after he was pulled against Tampa Bay, he made 34 saves on 37 shots and saved 1.57 goals more than they deserved. Charlie Lindgren, in relief, stopped 10 of 12.

Quinn, with two goals and an assist, keeps making his case in a contract year that has The New York Times asking what his next deal might cost. Buffalo now heads to Florida for a back-to-back against the Panthers and Lightning. Washington goes home to think about four losses in a row, and a third period that came about 40 minutes too late.
headline: Sabres score early, Ovechkin passes Backstrom late
